analysis:
Examined every supplied source, patch and metadata unit against the canonical index and selected definitions. The PR expands macOS CI routing to Darkbloom Sandboxes, with independent shard lanes. Visible consumers include .github/workflows/ci.yml:1072-1074 and 1134-1136. Changelog lines 3-6 and the build-guide patch describe classifier-selected requests, exact-label grants and Blacksmith fallback. These statements are not proof of the routing implementation.

The surrounding workflow retains pinned checkout/cache actions, persist-credentials:false, conditional cache saves and bounded jobs. GPU test failures remain nonblocking at ci.yml:1124; the range map shows this is unchanged. The Provider Tests gate at 1185-1217 checks classifier success and selected blocking-lane results. No supplied change alters provider authorization, attestation, inference encryption, billing or release qualification, and no concrete regression is established here.

Integration must reconcile routing with the reusable route workflow and provider-ci-build action: verify lane/count matching, fork exclusion, exact-label validation, job permissions and which caches routed push jobs can publish. Build.md BASE:181-186 and 221-240 describe distinct release qualification/cache contracts; confirm these remain isolated from products produced on the newly eligible runners. Sandbox host isolation and cache-writer trust matter given adversarial providers (ADV-001, TB-003) and qualified artifact identity (A-017, T-054), but the supplied evidence does not establish a compromised host, shared release cache or missing isolation control. These are unverified contracts, not findings. Full routing and build-action implementations are outside this batch, so the security conclusion needs integration review.
